summary: This bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to raise the maximum prison term for illegal entry from 2 to 5 years, impose a 5-year mandatory minimum on illegal entrants later convicted of any felony or crime punishable by over 1 year, and replace existing reentry penalties with new tiers that include a 10-year mandatory minimum for removed aliens previously convicted of an aggravated felony, any felony, or any crime punishable by over 1 year.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to government spending, appropriations, or budgetary changes. It solely amends criminal penalties under immigration law.
No references to taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation does not address healthcare policy, coverage, or markets in any way.
No provisions relate to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill directly amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to substantially increase criminal penalties for illegal entry (from 2 to 5 years) and reentry after removal (up to 10 years, with mandatory minimums of 10 years or more for those with prior convictions). It targets unlawful presence and reentry, explicitly aiming to deter and punish illegal immigration. This strongly aligns with restricting immigration and enforcing borders.
The bill has no connection to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions address military or defense spending or policy.
The legislation contains nothing related to environmental regulations or climate policy.
No references to welfare programs, food stamps, or social safety net policies.
The bill does not engage with education funding, schools, or choice programs.

While the bill references prior drug-related misdemeanors as a factor triggering enhanced immigration penalties, it does not alter drug laws, decriminalization, or enforcement priorities. The connection is incidental and does not constitute engagement with drug policy itself.

The bill increases maximum sentences, imposes mandatory minimum prison terms (5–10 years or life), and expands criminal liability for immigration violations, particularly for repeat offenders or those with prior convictions. This constitutes tougher sentencing measures in the criminal justice system.
No provisions relate to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill makes no reference to deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No content addresses LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
